hypotheses.construction_plan: Define the latent ordered two-slot kernel F(u,v)=T(u,v). Let P be the S2 permutation operator P[F(u,v)]=F(v,u). The term T(i,j) is the identity orbit representative F(i,j). Applying P gives T(j,i). The raw expression is the orbit sum F(i,j)+P[F(i,j)] over the two-element argument-permutation group.
required_assumptions: T has two distinguishable ordered argument slots so the swap u<->v is a nontrivial operator.
proof_obligations: T(i, j) - identity[F(u, v) with u=i, v=j] = 0
T(j, i) - permute[F(u, v) with u=i, v=j] = 0
hypotheses.rationale: The two non-identical subexpressions are the same applied function T with its two indices interchanged; the index swap is exactly the nontrivial S2 permutation action on the ordered argument slots. This represents the expression as a symmetrized orbit sum without introducing any leaf-substitution-only parameter family.
